items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: John Brown succeeded him. I succeeded John Brown.

ctx.x: Well now when I went to New Orleans I started putting that double beat on it like that.

We used to play it like a ragtime should be played. You see. Ought to be played those days. Of course the boys in New Orleans put a different touch on it. Scott Joplin presented Alonzo Hardy with the Maple Leaf Rag and these other three rags there and told him, well you can have these if you're playing for me. And Alonzo issued the parts out and said, well, we'll have to play it for you. Because there wasn't anything too tough for Alonzo Hardy. He was the first bandmaster I had been in the college. John Brown…

Well anyway, you've certainly explained a lot of things and directed a lot of false notions about music. I hope I have. I hope I have. Your broad experience is invaluable in being all over the country, which a lot of people have never had. That's right. Travel from one end of the country to the other and play and see everybody. Music all over the country. Thank you. It gives you a wonderful broad view of it.
